fields.title: Leading with "Yes, And"
fields.description: Would you like to lead an inclusive and collaborative group? Learn how basic improv techniques like "Yes, And" can be applied to enhance your group dynamic. "Yes, And" does not mean you need to agree with everything. In this workshop you will use active listening, being present, accepting and building a scene and discuss how that can be applied to enhance any group dynamic.

fields.bio: Xyla (she/her/hers) is a Business Solutions Senior Manager at Health Care Services Corporation. She works with clinical leads and IT architects to assess business case scope and requirements for funding approval and project delivery. Her interests include Toastmaters public speaking, producing, writing, impov and sketch comedy. A UIUC alum, she received her BA in Political Science, BS in Telecommunications Management and her MBA in Entrepreneurship from the Kellstadt Graduate School of Business at DePaul University.

fields.title: Youth on the March - History of Filipino Youth Activism
fields.description: We will educate attendees on the history of Filipino youth activism from the Philippines all the way to the diaspore all over the world. From Spanish Occupation to First Quarter Storm to modern day fights for education and migrant rights, Filipino youth have always been on the forefront of social change. We will also discuss the current day problems of Filipino youth and how we can begin to address them. We will equip attendees with easy steps and tools to be able to push for a better future for them and all the Filipino people and empower them to continue the tradition of Filipino youth pushing for change!

fields.facilitators: Megan Wikowsky, Anna Guieb, Jacob Belencion, Gabby Abacan, Rian Icao, Rua Figueroa, Yves Entereso
fields.bio: Anakbayan is a national democratic mass organization of the youth that aims to organize and mobilize Filipino youth for national democracy and to unify this movement with the powerful movement of the Filipino people all over the world. Anakbayan wages mass campaigns to take up the interests of the people. They also conduct education & studies on the history and current conditions of the Philippines.

fields.title: The "Isang Bagsak" Spirit in the Modern Day
fields.description: "Isang Bagsak", the unity clap born of anti-Martial Law activists and the United Farm Workers Movement of the 1960s, is an enduring symbol of solidarity in Filipino Culture. In short- if one falls, we all fall, but if one rises, we all rise. Now more than ever, as we see our kababayan face great and unprecedented injustices across the board, we'd like to discuss the concepts of solidarity and the importance of togetherness so that we together may not fall, but rise as one.

fields.facilitators: Lillian Tan, Ethan Lopez, Elise Gratz, Jenny Chotsuwan, Oishii Basu, Angelan Lin
fields.bio: The Asian American Coalition to Combat Oppression, Racism, and Discrimination (ACCORD) is an organization dedicated to advocating for social and political awareness as it relates to the Asian American experience at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Founded in 2024 by Ella Yoo, the organization seeks to emulate The Asian Pacific American Coalition (APAC) and other Asian American student movements at UIUC that built and shaped today's Asian American community. We seek to create spaces for dialogue and discovery surrounding the Asian American identity and various other intersecting identities, and to inspire action promoting and protecting the same.

fields.title: The Fight for Land in the Philippines: Supporting Indigenous Peoples and Peasant Struggles
fields.description:
There are over 120 indigenous groups in the Philippines with rich histories of resistance. However, despite this wide diversity, the stories of indigenous peoples in the Philippines are often erased and silenced. Furthermore, the Philippine government has increasingly invested in development projects that are stripping indigenous people of their ancestral land, crucial natural resources, and increasing the level of military surveillance and violence in their communities. 

Mary Manching, along with other members of Anakbayan Chicago and Kabataan Alliance, will share the lessons and stories they learned from their recent exposure trip to the Philippines, where they integrated with indigenous peoples and peasant communities. This sharing of stories aims to push youth to question who the development projects in the Philippines currently serve and what development that actually serves the needs of the indigenous people could look like. This workshop will also shed light on the ways that indigenous people and peasant people in the Philippines are fighting back and what youth in the US can do to support them in the fight for a more sustainable, self-determined future. Join us for a session of meaningful discussion and even some music-making.

fields.facilitators: Mary Gabrielle Manching, Craig Ymson, Lukas Nepomuceno
fields.bio: Mary Gabrielle Manching is the proud daughter of Filipino immigrants, coming from Bicol and Cebu, Philippines. Her family’s immigration story inspires her to fight for a world in which my family, my friends’ families, and our future generations no longer have to struggle to find their home. Mary is captivated by the radical love and community care that community organizing spaces emanate and aspires to continue working on campaign strategy for immigrant rights community organizations in the near future. She is currently a member of Anakbayan Chicago-an organization dedicated to building collective youth power for a national democratic society in the Philippines.

fields.title: What’s Your Istorya?
fields.description: If Origins helps us remember where we come from, What’s Your Istorya? invites us to explore how we carry those stories forward. Through food, storytelling, and reflection, participants learn how lived experience can guide creativity and leadership. With pakikipagkwentuhan (story-sharing rooted in connection) as the guiding practice, the session offers tools to support each participant’s storytelling journey. Participants identify the form of expression that feels most natural to them and explore how culture, creativity, and care come together in every act of storytelling.

fields.bio: Istorya is a Filipino storytelling initiative that explores the Philippines’ history through food and shared narrative. Founded by Walbert Castillo and co-led with Monica Blanco, Istorya transforms cultural research into immersive dining and educational experiences. Their work bridges food, identity, and agency, revealing how Filipinos have continually created, adapted, and resisted through honoring their palates. Through workshops and pop-ups, Istorya helps communities reconnect with culture and proclaim their stories with pride.

fields.title: [CANCELLED] Combatting Imposter Phenomenon
fields.description: Imposter Phenomenon is often used to describe internal experiences of intellectual phoniness that appears to be particularly prevalent and intense among a select sample of high achieving women. This interactive workshop will explore the common ways imposter syndrome shows up and ways to combat it in our lives.

fields.bio: Amie is a two time alumna of the University of Illinois, having earned a B.A. in English and a M.Ed in Education Policy, Organization and Leadership with a concentration in Diversity & Equity in Education. As an undergraduate student, Amie worked at the Women’s Resources Center as peer educator for the First Year Consent and Relationship Education (FYCARE) Program.  In her role at the WRC, Amie leads the efforts to explore gender equity across all its many intersections and support the leadership of students of all genders as they work to improve campus climate and promote gender justice worldwide.

fields.title: BITAW: Unleashing Voices through Cultural Activism
fields.description:
Join us for BITAW: Unleashing Voices through Cultural Activism, an innovative workshop that combines integrated theatre arts with interactive storytelling to explore identity and community. This engaging experience will foster dynamic conversations in a safe space, encouraging participants to express their unique narratives through various artistic methods.

The workshop features activities such as Pepe and Pilar drawing, a mini flash fiction session, and image theatre, allowing attendees to visualize and articulate their stories creatively. Through collaborative exercises, participants will not only deepen their understanding of cultural identity but also build connections within the community. Whether you are an experienced artist or a curious newcomer, this workshop invites everyone to discover the transformative power of storytelling and cultural expression. Come ready to share, create, and connect!

fields.bio: CIRCA Pintig is a Chicago-based arts and community organization with a rich history spanning 35 years. Established to promote education, advocacy, and community organizing through theater, it produces creative works that reflect the Filipino American experience. The organization is dedicated to amplifying diverse voices and tackling social issues through powerful productions. Recent projects include Krossroad the Musical, which follows a Filipina nurse's journey (September 2025), the 2nd Annual Chicago Filipino American Theatre Festival featuring various playwrights (October 2025), and a touring production of Panther in the Sky, addressing senseless gun violence.

fields.title: Acing Your Interview : Make an Impression, Get the Offer!
fields.description: In a time where the job market is competitive and AI has deeply impacted the job search process, making a strong impression during your interview is key.  Whether you are looking for internships or full time work, join this session to learn strategies and tools to effectively prepare, make a lasting impression while presenting yourself authentically, negotiate salary, and get the most out of your interview opportunities.

fields.bio: James Castree currently serves as Senior Assistant Director at the Career Center at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.  He has over a decade of higher education experience at schools ranging from local community colleges to flagship Research I institutions.  James holds degrees in Psychology and in Education, Policy, Organization, & Leadership from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

fields.title: History, Harmony and Heart: The Great Filipino Songbook Movement
fields.description:
"Lou Ella Rose brings to life pivotal moments in Filipino American and Asian American history through the songs and stories of legendary Filipino composers—some with significant ties to Chicago and the Midwest, like Nicanor Abelardo, Francisco Santiago, and the Philippine Constabulary Band. This workshop celebrates traditional Filipino music—Kundiman, Balitaw, Danza, and Folk Songs—and its role in shaping Filipino identity, featuring rare photos, sound clips, pre-war films, early recordings, and reimagined works by her band, SamaSama Project. 

Aligned with FACT 2025’s theme, “Ipahayag nang Malakas,” attendees will explore how ancestral music empowers us today and how we can reclaim and amplify our history in the face of cultural erasure. 

The TGFS movement has received recognition and support from institutions, including the Asian Cultural Council Fellowship, DCASE Grant, Chicago Park District NOITP program, and the UIC Convocation Series, highlighting both its cultural impact and opportunities for engagement. Participants—artists, designers, event managers, photographers, filmmakers, writers, and tech developers—are invited to explore how they can be part of the movement to leverage TGFS’s current visibility and support in enriching and expanding the Filipino arts community in the Midwest and beyond."

fields.bio: An Asian Cultural Council Fellow and a Chicago DCASE Individual Artist Program Grantee for 2024, Lou Ella Rose is the lead singer/Creative Director of Filipino folk fusion band, SamaSama Project performing at concerts and festivals in the Midwest and the World Youth Day in Madrid, Spain. A seasoned musical theater actor in Manila and Singapore, she appeared on TV soap operas, live shows, and viral TV commercials in Asia and was selected as one of Chicago Cabaret Professionals' Emerging Artists in 2022. The progenitor of The Great Filipino Songbook (TGFS), she brings to life the rich traditions of Filipino music on the intimate stage, captivating audiences and fostering a deeper appreciation for the cultural contributions of Filipino Americans. She’s one of 10 inaugural delegates of the Filipino Young Leaders Program and serves on the board of Asian Popup Cinema and PACCGC (Fil Am Chamber of Commerce). She is mama to Reign and life-long partner to Baron and finds that most fulfilling.

fields.title: Building Generational Wealth not Trauma
fields.description: “Building Generational Wealth, Not Trauma” is a workshop designed to help Filipino American students break cycles of financial stress and start building lasting wealth. We’ll unpack the cultural habits that often hold our community back—and have uncomfortable discussions about money we’re often scared to have. Students will learn the essentials of personal finance, including credit cards, budgeting, savings accounts, 401(k)s, and brokerage basics, through approachable and real-world examples. The session will also cover career development topics like job searching, interviewing with confidence, and negotiating your first salary. More than just a finance talk, this is a space to reflect on how we can honor our families while creating healthier, more empowered futures. Together, we’ll explore how to build not just wealth, but legacy—with heart, intention, and community in mind.

fields.bio: Michael Corrales is a recent graduate of the University of Illinois where he studied Supply Chain Management and International Business. Michael graduated with Senior 100 honors awarded to the top 100 wholistic seniors in the entire school. Michael has interned at Elevate Energy as well as Bp the last two years where he know works full time in the Graduate Development Program. Michael served as the director of Professional Development for several RSO’s while on campus  as well as a peer mentor for the Gies college of business.

fields.title: Beyond Personal Cultural Connections: Joining the Fight for a Just World for Indigenous People Communities
fields.description: PCNs and Battle of the Bamboo are often highlights of the college experience for Filipino students in  the Midwest. With so many dances hailing from indigenous groups in the Philippines, this workshop challenges us to look beyond our own journey of connection to culture and towards being a part of fighting for a just world for everyone, including indigenous peoples in the Philippines. Just coming back from an exposure trip to the Philippines, facilitators will share the lessons and stories on how the indigenous peoples and peasant communities they integrated with in the Philippines are fighting back.This workshop will hold space for students to brainstorm together how students who already engage in PCNs and Battle can learn more about the people behind the dances. Students will be empowered to develop critical tools and leadership skills needed to continue the education and build collective power in solidarity with indigenous people and peasant communities and their fight for a more sustainable, self-determined future.

fields.facilitators: Mary Gabrielle Manching, Craig Ymson, Lukas Nepomuceno
fields.bio: Mary Gabrielle Manching is the proud daughter of Filipino immigrants, coming from Bicol and Cebu, Philippines. Her family’s immigration story inspires her to fight for a world in which my family, my friends’ families, and our future generations no longer have to struggle to find their home. Mary is captivated by the radical love and community care that community organizing spaces emanate and aspires to continue working on campaign strategy for immigrant rights community organizations in the near future. She is currently a member of Anakbayan Chicago-an organization dedicated to building collective youth power for a national democratic society in the Philippines.

fields.title: The Business of Being an Artist: What I Learned Transitioning from a Corporate Professional to a Full-Time Artist
fields.description:
"In this engaging and interactive session, Lou Ella Rose shares her journey from corporate professional to full-time artist — the challenges, mindset shifts, and practical strategies that helped her thrive as a musician and creative entrepreneur.

Participants will explore how to balance artistic passion with professional sustainability, develop essential business and networking skills, and adopt a growth mindset that supports both personal fulfillment and career longevity.

The workshop also introduces the Musika SamaSama Artists Community, an inclusive network that empowers Filipino and Filipino American artists through collaboration, mentorship, and shared creative practice.

By the end of the session, participants will:
- Identify key skills needed to sustain and grow an artistic career
- Reflect on the mindset shifts necessary for long-term creative success
- Learn tools for branding, organization, and leveraging grants or funding opportunities
- Connect with a supportive community of artists dedicated to collective growth and visibility"

fields.bio: An Asian Cultural Council Fellow and a Chicago DCASE Individual Artist Program Grantee for 2024, Lou Ella Rose is the lead singer/Creative Director of Filipino folk fusion band, SamaSama Project performing at concerts and festivals in the Midwest and the World Youth Day in Madrid, Spain. A seasoned musical theater actor in Manila and Singapore, she appeared on TV soap operas, live shows, and viral TV commercials in Asia and was selected as one of Chicago Cabaret Professionals' Emerging Artists in 2022. The progenitor of The Great Filipino Songbook (TGFS), she brings to life the rich traditions of Filipino music on the intimate stage, captivating audiences and fostering a deeper appreciation for the cultural contributions of Filipino Americans. She’s one of 10 inaugural delegates of the Filipino Young Leaders Program and serves on the board of Asian Popup Cinema and PACCGC (Fil Am Chamber of Commerce). She is mama to Reign and life-long partner to Baron and finds that most fulfilling.

fields.title: Intersectionality of Identity: how do our identities interact and how do you feel "in between?"
fields.description: Intersectionality in this context is how different aspects of our identity like race, gender, class, ethnicity, and ability interact with each other to shape who we are through our unique experiences. In this workshop, we will explore what that means for each of us through small group discussions about how the various categories affect each other in our lives, sometimes in ways we don't usually think about. We will also consider our identities as Asian Americans, what that means to us, and the ways we align or don't align with how others consider that to look like. The label of Asian American does not fully capture how generation, family origin, community, and connection to culture come together to allow for a rich spectrum of experiences. We hope to provide an interesting perspective on how our identities influence our lived experiences, and how that in turn affects who we are!

fields.facilitators: Milan Monroe, Carissa Westphal, Grace Monago, Sophie Bush, Sophie Reck, Angelan Lin
fields.bio: In Between is a social-cultural club that focuses on Asian Americans and Adoptees who don’t strongly identify with their Asian or American cultures/identities. We foster a smaller but inclusive community on campus through a variety of events! We host semi-formal Round Table discussion events on topics relating to Asian American identity such as media, holidays, interpersonal connections, intersectionality (how different parts of our identity interact with each other), and the feeling of being "in between". Through our Adoptee Socials and Conversation Tables, we create a space on campus for adoptees and those who want to learn about the adoptee experience. We also do craft nights, potlucks, and collaborations with other Asian-interest organizations on campus!

fields.title: Empowerment for the Imperfect
fields.description: There always seems to be someone faster, stronger, smarter. And sometimes you feel yourself hitting your limits when you see that job ahead of you. Should you step aside to let someone more qualified do the work? Do you ever feel like you're not quite... enough? You wouldn't be alone. Let's redefine adequacy and qualification with the imperfection of being a normal person.

fields.bio: Jeremy Bautista received his Bachelor of Arts in History from UIUC in 1996 and his Master of Arts in Teaching from National-Louis in 1999. During undergrad, he served as External Vice President for PSA and Co-Director of APAC (Asian Pacific American Coalition). He also helped direct the first Filipino American Students Conference at UIUC, which eventually was renamed FACT and continues today. He currently works in K-12 education in the Chicago suburb of Westmont, IL in the CUSD 201 Technology Department. He also works with student groups such as co-sponsoring the club CAPAOW (the Club of Asian and Pacific Americans Of Westmont), the first Asian American student club of Westmont High School.

fields.title: Origins: Remembering Where We Come From
fields.description: Filipino history is often taught through dates and names, but it also lives in kitchens, recipes, and shared meals. This session introduces Istorya’s founding story and how tracing history through food became a way to rebuild belonging and cultural memory. Participants explore how food, memory, and migration shape identity and connection across generations. Using pakikipagkwentuhan (story-sharing rooted in connection), participants reflect on how their own stories contribute to a collective narrative of Filipino creativity and care. Together, we map personal constellations that link memory, identity, and community.

fields.bio: Istorya is a Filipino storytelling initiative that explores the Philippines’ history through food and shared narrative. Founded by Walbert Castillo and co-led with Monica Blanco, Istorya transforms cultural research into immersive dining and educational experiences. Their work bridges food, identity, and agency, revealing how Filipinos have continually created, adapted, and resisted through honoring their palates. Through workshops and pop-ups, Istorya helps communities reconnect with culture and proclaim their stories with pride.

fields.title: Ito ang Kuwento Ko: Getting to Know Your Inner Filipino through Basic Creative Writing Principles
fields.description: This workshop explores basic creative writing principles, such as finding inspirations towards a story concept, creating your character, and drafting a manuscript outline. Through activities that allow you to unleash your inner cultural identity as a Filipino, the goal in this workshop is to use your own journey from homeland to diaspora as a way to not only create a story concept but to also understand yourself more as a Filipino/Filipino American, so that you can champion your identities in various spaces.

fields.bio: Cheeno Marlo M. Sayuno, PhD, is a Postdoctoral Research Associate at the School of Information Sciences, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, and an Associate Professor of Communication, Research, and Children’s Literature from the University of the Philippines (UP) Los Baños. He is also a published picturebook author and has written journal articles and book chapters for international journals and collections. He has received recognition in the Philippines, such as the prestigious Carlos Palanca Memorial Awards for Literature, the National Book Awards, the Philippine Board on Books for Young People’s Salanga Prize, and the Normal Awards for Gender-Inclusive Literature by Philippine Normal University. His research interests include transmedia studies and digital storytelling, and children’s literature, media, and culture.

fields.title: Listening First: A Closer Look at Our Communities
fields.description: Angelo Battung, Arhys Ocupe, Rydel Salazar, and Princess Yara Luis were participants of the PUSO Foundation’s 2025 Immersion Program in the Philippines. During the program, they engaged with local communities to better understand the stories, challenges, and resilience of the people PUSO serves. Through this experience, they gained a deeper awareness of social and systemic issues such as access to healthcare, education, or poverty alleviation, and learned the importance of listening with empathy before taking action. They hope to continue fostering awareness and compassion through future service and advocacy efforts inspired by the communities served through The PUSO Foundation.

fields.facilitators: Angelo Battung, Matthew Villalon, Lauren Dimayuga, Rydel Salazar, Princess Yara Luis, Inaki Azcueta, Arhys Ocupe, LJ Hanyzewski
fields.bio: The Purposeful Unconditional Service to Others is a 501 (c)(3) Non-Profit Organization with the mission of providing hope with a purpose. Our desire is to empower individuals to be involved in service work through the gift of giving back. When a community comes together, we can accomplish just about anything. By raising funds through our annual fundraising events, college outreach program, and various campaigns – we are able to strategically allocate financial contributions to impoverished communities, schools, communal projects and our relief efforts around the world.

fields.title: Lessons from Filipinx Social Media Content Creators.
fields.description: This workshop will ask participants to examine Filipinx YouTube and Facebook videos and reflect on their own practices of social media consumption. The participants will also have the opportunity to share, discuss, and think critically about their favorite social media content creators. In a time when we are bombarded with mis/dis/information from many levels and sources of information, how might we think about the limits and political potential of social media? And what can our diverse social media consumption practices teach us about how to navigate these spaces differently?

fields.bio: Dr. David G. Siglos Jr. received his Ph.D. in English at the University of California, Riverside. He is currently a lecturer in the Department of Asian American Studies at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign. His book project, entitled Filipino Style: Salvaging the Novel and the U.S. Empire, explores contemporary Filipino American novels to describe the life-making strategies and creative tactics of Filipinos, what he calls “Filipino style of being.” The project thinks about the Filipino culture as a style to account for its aesthetic production, which he argues defies global capitalist logics of development, modernity, and progress. David’s research interests include 20th – 21st century American and Asian American Literature, Filipino Anglophone Literature, Postcolonial Theory, Global Modernism, Nationalism and Narrative, Media, Film, and Culture Studies, and Theater and Performance.

fields.title: Awareness of PSAs in the Midwest, What is the MAFA-Sphere?
fields.description: This workshop is dedicated to raising awareness and fostering community among Philippine Student Organizations in MAFA. Through dialogue and collaboration, we aim to highlight the importance of cultural identity, as well as explain what MAFA offers. Participants will have the opportunity to connect, and meet new friends! Together, we strive to build lasting networks that empower future leaders and celebrate Filipino heritage.

fields.facilitators: Spencer Ainza, Erika Bando, Jaden Sebastian, Jordan Cruz, Michael Massey, Juliana Grageda, Julia Domingo, Aria Garcia, Kimberlie Saldana, Chloe Desierto
fields.bio: The Midwest Association of Filipino-Americans exists to promote unity and cooperation amongst Filipinos and Filipino Americans around the Midwest and beyond by promoting Filipino culture and Asian American awareness, coordinating meetings and events, and supporting the objectives of the MAFA Member Organizations. MAFA operates as a charitable organization in order to fulfill its mission and provide resources to other charitable organizations that align with MAFA’s mission and values.

fields.title: Youth on the March - History of Filipino Youth Activism
fields.description: We will educate attendees on the history of Filipino youth activism from the Philippines all the way to the diaspore all over the world. From Spanish Occupation to First Quarter Storm to modern day fights for education and migrant rights, Filipino youth have always been on the forefront of social change. We will also discuss the current day problems of Filipino youth and how we can begin to address them. We will equip attendees with easy steps and tools to be able to push for a better future for them and all the Filipino people and empower them to continue the tradition of Filipino youth pushing for change!

Anakbayan wages mass campaigns to take up the interests of the people. They also conduct education & studies on the history and current conditions of the Philippines.

fields.title: Defend Filipino Migrants
fields.description: In this workshop, we will introduce the situation for Filipino migrants and educate on how we can navigate the current political climate. We will introduce what isTanggol Migrante Movement as the alliance of organizations commited to advocating for the rights and welfare of Filipino migrants. Our goal is to educate Filipino youth on easy ways to support migrants like Know Your Rights and fundraisers to support Filipino migrants. We will also discuss how we can unite as Filipino youth to continue advocating for our the wellbeing of our families, friends, and communities.

fields.facilitators: John Emiliano, Matt Martirez, LJ Hanyzewski, Ray Cave, Faith Cabalfin
fields.bio:
Kabataan Alliance is a national alliance of more than 50 Filipino youth and student organizations dedicated to serving our communities in the U.S. and back home in the Philippines.  

To build national unity among Filipino youth across the United States to advocate for the rights and welfare of Filipinos in the US, the Philippines, and around the world.

We unite and empower Filipino youth across the U.S. to engage in community organizing and advocacy to build towards a just society where people can reach their full potentials.

fields.title: Voices of Empowerment: Building Community Through Music
fields.description: Our workshop explores how music can be used as a tool for empowerment and collective expression. Through discussion, song analysis, and collaborative activities, attendees will reflect on the role music plays in social movements and personal empowerment. We will highlight songs that confront issues such as oppression, corruption, and social hierarchy, while also celebrating resilience and community. Participants will work in small groups to create and present their own short arrangements of empowering songs, supported by Harana members and instrumentalists. By the end, attendees will leave with a stronger sense of how music connects us and inspires action.

fields.facilitators: Rain Seriosa, Rochelle Anne Sazon, Daniel De Guzman
fields.bio: PSA Harana is the musical subgroup under the Philippine Student Association at UIUC composed of talented and passionate musicians! While “harana” may translate to serenading, the term refers more specifically to the act of serenading as a form of courtship. This tradition originates from pre-colonial to colonial Philippines and allowed for the passing down of oral traditions through song. Harana aims to share Filipinx culture and bring together a community of people who share a love for music!

fields.title: FAMT Idea-thon
fields.description: Join FAMT for an interactive Ideathon designed to help participants develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges from our hackathon Kapwa Codefest. This session will guide attendees through a problem-solving framework, breaking complex issues into manageable steps and transforming abstract ideas into actionable concepts. Teams will have the opportunity to pitch their ideas to hackathon winners from the FAMT team, receive constructive feedback, and connect with peers during a dedicated networking session.

fields.facilitators: Jordan Cruz, Kieran Llarena, Benson Manzano, Kirk Caponpon
fields.bio:
Filipino Americans in Tech is an organization that aims to help Filipinos (specifically college students, but not limited to) advance into the tech industry. We do this by providing our community with: a job board (that is updated nearly instantaneously when a new job posting is made, crowd-sourced channel of opportunities, a network of Filipinos from different backgrounds in tech (Big Tech / Industry, startups, etc.), resume roast board.

What we’re currently working on for the future is: mentorship, Supplemental educational courses like programming, Kapwa Codefest 2025, a hackathon to celebrate Filipino American History Month by supporting local Filipino businesses in the United States

In the past, we’ve hosted events and individuals from many different companies, like Google, TikTok, Amazon, Dreamhaven

fields.title: Telling My Leadership Story
fields.description: What makes one an authentic leader? By telling personal leadership stories, people reflect on different aspects of leadership such as their values and beliefs, their goals, the actions that they take to achieve those goals, and why their role as a leader is important. In this workshop, participants will learn the purpose of telling their leadership stories and how to tell a story that represents their purpose as a leader. Participants will be able to draft and practice telling their story in a way that highlights who they are as a leader.

fields.bio: Our work is to study about leadership and teach students the relevant skills to be effective leaders, so they can make positive impacts for society! We believe leaders are individuals who work with others to make positive change. Leadership development begins with self-knowledge. Leadership never happens alone. Leadership is exercised as members of teams, business, civic and community organizations, and as global citizens. Our goal is to help Illinois students become better leaders through our programming and services.

fields.title: Work In Progress: The Evolution of Confidence as a Woman
fields.description: Josie Liu shares her ongoing journey of personal growth as a woman learning to navigate confidence, sexuality, and self-expression in a world of double standards. Growing up in a purity culture household, Josie entered college determined to unlearn internalized sexism and redefine her relationship with womanhood, confidence, and modern-day feminism. Through experiences of self-discovery, from challenging beauty norms to exploring sexual agency and leading spaces of empowerment, she’s learned that growth is not linear, but deeply personal. This workshop invites participants to reflect on their own journeys, confront societal expectations, and embrace confidence and authenticity on their own terms.

fields.bio: Josie Liu grew up as an extremely shy and closed off child but has spent her high school and college years gaining her confidence and redefining what it means to be a woman navigating double standards and societal expectations. After being rejected from the Fashion Network her first semester, she created her own modeling opportunity and later shaved her head in attempt to detach her self-worth from appearance. Through joining a sorority, founding an anti-human trafficking organization, and working at the Women’s Resource Center, Josie has learned the power of sisterhood, advocacy, and using her voice. Every project she’s taken on, from starting rock bands to opening a live music venue, has strengthened her confidence, challenged norms, and deepened her commitment to empowering women to embrace their individuality.

fields.title: Proclaim Your Path: Translating Vision into Sustainable Action
fields.description: How do you turn good intentions into real, sustained action? In this interactive session, educator and strategist Melorie Serrano Masacupan, M.Ed. guides participants through a structured reflection process that transforms vision into accountability. You’ll articulate where you want to be three years from now, identify key focus areas for the year ahead, and craft concrete SMART goals to move you forward. Through collaborative coaching and peer accountability trios, you’ll leave not only with clear goals but also with a built-in support system to keep you on track. Participants receive three optional check-ins with the facilitator over the next year to sustain growth and celebrate progress.

fields.bio: Melorie Serrano Masacupan, M.Ed is an educator, strategist, and storyteller with over 15 years of experience designing learning experiences that foster equity, reflection, and sustainable growth. Her career spans teaching, nonprofit leadership, and communications—bridging practice, policy, and public understanding to drive systems-level change. Melorie has partnered with education and social impact organizations to strengthen leadership pipelines, align strategy with values, and create cultures of accountability rooted in care. As a facilitator and coach, she blends structured reflection with actionable follow-up to help individuals and teams translate insight into lasting change. She is currently training as a Spelling to Communicate (S2C) practitioner, deepening her commitment to expanding voice and agency for future advocates.

fields.title: Healing Through Service
fields.description: We will explore how acts of service can nurture personal growth, mental health, and a deeper sense of identity. Rooted in The PUSO Foundation’s mission of hope, purpose, and community, this session invites participants to reflect on the heart behind service and the stories of those impacted by PUSO’s work. Through reflection, dialogue, and making letters, participants will see how serving others helps strengthen empathy and community. This workshop encourages attendees to connect their own journeys of identity and well-being to the collective spirit of service that defines PUSO.

fields.facilitators: Angelo Battung, Matthew Villalon, Lauren Dimayuga, Rydel Salazar, Princess Yara Luis, Inaki Azcueta, Arhys Ocupe, LJ Hanyzewski
fields.bio: The Purposeful Unconditional Service to Others is a 501 (c)(3) Non-Profit Organization with the mission of providing hope with a purpose. Our desire is to empower individuals to be involved in service work through the gift of giving back. When a community comes together, we can accomplish just about anything. By raising funds through our annual fundraising events, college outreach program, and various campaigns – we are able to strategically allocate financial contributions to impoverished communities, schools, communal projects and our relief efforts around the world.

fields.title: By the Grace of Us: Finding True Self
fields.description: In this interactive workshop, learn how to identify the values that you hold most dear, to give yourself more grace, be more present, and practice self-awareness. In a world that gets increasingly tough, being kind to each other is helpful, but being kind to ourselves is underestimated. This is especially true with the pressures of school, Filipinx family life, and finding your community. Creativity, mindfulness, and reflection can help identify your personal values, which can act as your northern star on your journey through life.

fields.bio:
Ryan Viloria (he/him) currently serves as the Fund Development Officer of the Rizal Center, Chicago's only Filipino community center, and as a freelance grants manager and writer. From 2019 - 2024, Ryan was the Executive Director of the Alliance of Filipinos for Immigrant Rights and Empowerment (AFIRE). He also served as a staff member for the Institute for Research on Race and Public Policy at the University of Illinois at Chicago. In 2015, Ryan served as the National Conference Coordinator for the National Queer Asian Pacific Islander Alliance (NQAPIA), and in 2019 he received NQAPIA's 2019 Midwest Community Catalyst Award.

In his spare time, Ryan enjoys walks on the beach, watching Star Trek, playing pool, and trying out new recipes.

fields.title: Intersectionality of Identity: how do our identities interact and how do you feel "in between?"
fields.description: Intersectionality in this context is how different aspects of our identity like race, gender, class, ethnicity, and ability interact with each other to shape who we are through our unique experiences. In this workshop, we will explore what that means for each of us through small group discussions about how the various categories affect each other in our lives, sometimes in ways we don't usually think about. We will also consider our identities as Asian Americans, what that means to us, and the ways we align or don't align with how others consider that to look like. The label of Asian American does not fully capture how generation, family origin, community, and connection to culture come together to allow for a rich spectrum of experiences. We hope to provide an interesting perspective on how our identities influence our lived experiences, and how that in turn affects who we are!

fields.facilitators: Milan Monroe, Carissa Westphal, Grace Monago, Sophie Bush, Sophie Reck, Angelan Lin
fields.bio: In Between is a social-cultural club that focuses on Asian Americans and Adoptees who don’t strongly identify with their Asian or American cultures/identities. We foster a smaller but inclusive community on campus through a variety of events! We host semi-formal Round Table discussion events on topics relating to Asian American identity such as media, holidays, interpersonal connections, intersectionality (how different parts of our identity interact with each other), and the feeling of being "in between". Through our Adoptee Socials and Conversation Tables, we create a space on campus for adoptees and those who want to learn about the adoptee experience. We also do craft nights, potlucks, and collaborations with other Asian-interest organizations on campus!

fields.title: Becoming: The Journey of Conscious Growth
fields.description: This workshop invites you to slow down, look within, and consciously design who you are becoming. Through practical psychology and self-discovery, it will guide you to release old stories, uncover the patterns that hold you back to re-align you with your values and create growth that is authentic, genuine and long lasting.

fields.bio: Geri Hernandez is the co-founder of Savory Crust. She founded the company with her sister, Jennifer. Both are Fil-Am women owned company that has a long history of cooking in their family. Savory Crust started in 2017 with the simple idea of bringing Filipino inspired empanadas and rice bowls to their neighborhood.

fields.title: Finding Common Ground
fields.description: How do you incorporate Integrative Thinking in an increasingly polarized world? In this workshop we will discuss the important aspects of healthy debate: Face to Face, Separate the Idea from Person, Embrace humility of uncertainty. There will be a 20 minute group interactive mind-mapping activity that provides an opportunity for participants to share personal ideas about a broad topic.

fields.bio: Xyla (she/her/hers) is a Business Solutions Senior Manager at Health Care Services Corporation. She works with clinical leads and IT architects to assess business case scope and requirements for funding approval and project delivery. Her interests include Toastmaters public speaking, producing, writing, impov and sketch comedy. A UIUC alum, she received her BA in Political Science, BS in Telecommunications Management and her MBA in Entrepreneurship from the Kellstadt Graduate School of Business at DePaul University.

fields.title: Entering the Workforce
fields.description: As recent post grads from UIUC, learn from their relevant experience on how to enter the workforce and make your mark on recruiters, managers, and fellow colleagues. This workshop will include resume, interview, and networking tips.

fields.bio:
Kaia Hsu recently graduated from UIUC majoring in actuarial science and minoring in communications in May 2025. She currently works for a Sammons Financial Group as an Actuarial Associate I. On campus, she was involved in Philippine Student Association, Beta Alpha Psi, and Actuarial Science Club. 
Andre Garcia graduated in the class of Spring 2024 with a double major in Supply Chain Management and Information Systems with a minor in Computer Science. Currently, he is working within Technology Consulting at EY's Chicago office. On campus, he was involved with Ascend Pan-Asian Leaders, Supply Chain Management Association, Mi Pueblo, and Philippine Student Association and CS105 Course Assistance.

fields.title: Demystifying Graduate School for Filipino-Americans
fields.description: Are you hoping to navigate the confusing graduate school process with confidence? In this workshop, I will break down the application, discuss potential funding opportunities such as fellowships, and explore how to find programs that align with your academic and career goals. We will discuss the different types of graduate degrees, how to build your network academically, and opportunities to take advantage of prior to applying. Whether you are the first in your family to pursue advanced education or just looking for community and guidance, this workshop will give you the advice and tools you need to pursue your graduate school aspirations. If you are attending this workshop, please fill out this form so I can best tailor this workshop for you: https://forms.gle/hGSaj2S3MFLCwuhn7

fields.bio: Ryan Talusan is a 2nd-year Bioengineering Ph.D. Student at the University of Washington. He graduated from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign in 2024 with a BS in Bioengineering and has spent time researching across multiple institutions (UIC, Northwestern, & NIMS Japan). As a PSA UIUC member, he was formerly Cultural, Vice President External, FCN Co-Chair, and Head of PSA Modern. Currently, his work focuses on synthesizing innovative biomaterial platforms for improving the delivery and storage of gene-based therapeutics. Outside of research, he spends his time balancing between mentoring high school/undergraduate students and participating in dance cyphers.

fields.title: Maximizing Your Career Fair Experience
fields.description: Attending a career fair is an important step in finding an internship or full-time position. Many higher educational institutions host a variety of career fairs throughout the school year, and we know they can feel overwhelming—especially if it’s your first time. This introductory workshop is designed for students who are new to career fairs or just beginning to explore their career options. You’ll learn what to expect, how to craft an effective elevator pitch, navigate employer booths with confidence, and follow up with employers after the event. You’ve got this!

fields.bio:
Zella Walden is an Assistant Director of Career Education and Outreach at the University of Illinois Career Center. Originally, a visiting research specialist for diagnostic testing she pivoted her career into career development after graduating with her master's in Agriculture Leadership, Education, and Communication. She oversees and trains undergraduates student workers, the Career Services Paraprofessionals, who deliver 3000+ cover letter, curriculum vitae, and resume reviews every academic year and facilitate career development workshops. She also serves as a certified career services provider providing additional support as a career coach and designing career development curriculum. 

She holds memberships with the National Association of Colleges and Employers and National Career Development Association.

fields.title: Defend Filipino Migrants
fields.description: In this workshop, we will introduce the situation for Filipino migrants and educate on how we can navigate the current political climate. We will introduce what isTanggol Migrante Movement as the alliance of organizations commited to advocating for the rights and welfare of Filipino migrants. Our goal is to educate Filipino youth on easy ways to support migrants like Know Your Rights and fundraisers to support Filipino migrants. We will also discuss how we can unite as Filipino youth to continue advocating for our the wellbeing of our families, friends, and communities.

fields.facilitators: John Emiliano, Matt Martirez, LJ Hanyzewski, Ray Cave, Faith Cabalfin
fields.bio:
Kabataan Alliance is a national alliance of more than 50 Filipino youth and student organizations dedicated to serving our communities in the U.S. and back home in the Philippines.  

To build national unity among Filipino youth across the United States to advocate for the rights and welfare of Filipinos in the US, the Philippines, and around the world.

We unite and empower Filipino youth across the U.S. to engage in community organizing and advocacy to build towards a just society where people can reach their full potentials.

fields.title: Thriving with Intention
fields.description: Thriving with Intention is an interactive workshop designed to help delegates reflect and reconnect with their sense of purpose. Through engaging activities and discussions, attendees will reflect on how balance, resilience, and personal growth can shape their daily lives. The session offers simple, practical tools to create an open space, restore energy, and move forward at their own pace.

fields.bio: Hahnbit Lee is a UIUC alum and current Doctoral Occupational Therapy student at Midwestern University. Through her studies, she explores how balance, flexibility, and therapeutic communication can support holistic well-being. She is passionate about empowering others to find meaning in their daily lives. Hahnbit values cultural humility and authentic self-expression as foundations for healing and building resilience through intentional growth.
